rows.note: All 3 attempts of a retried GET carry byte-identical heads: request line with query, Host, X-Forwarded-For, client headers, .requestHeader value, one Connection: close.
Over TinyHttpd the third 503 is relayed with its own Retry-After, both X-Multi lines and its chunked body; nothing of attempts 0 and 1 leaks.
Over a TinyHttpd socket a bodyless GET and a GET with Content-Length: 0 each arrive 3 times.
Over TinyHttpd a keep-open Content-Length backend answers the client promptly and the next request on .maxConcurrent(1) reaches the backend (the existing AC-4 test covers the in-memory adapter only).

With retries(5), retryDelay 600 ms and totalTimeout 1000 ms, an always-503 backend sees 2 arrivals and the second 503 is relayed at once with no error. A first version (delay 400 ms) was red only because this host's JVM oversleeps: Thread.sleep(400) measured 495-549 ms and the scheduler fires late by the same amount, so the third attempt started at about 1.1 s. That is host timer slack, not a defect: the code checks the nominal wait against the deadline as the requirement states. The test was retuned to leave margin for that slack.

During a retry wait on .maxConcurrent(1), a concurrent request gets 503 CONCURRENCY_LIMIT with no backend connection. The retried request still makes exactly 3 attempts and the slot is free afterwards (FR-PROXY-019).
After a POST retried on refused connects ends in 502, the watchdog queue is empty (REL-PROXY-002), so no reservation or write deadline leaks per attempt.
Connect attempts after refused connections are at least retryDelay (300 ms) apart; 3 attempts end in 502.
Over TinyHttpd a chunked POST body arrives whole on the third connect after two refused connects.
Under retryUnsafeMethods(true).retries(1), a bodyless POST (503) and a bodyless PUT (502), both sent with Content-Length: 0, each arrive twice.
With a keep-alive 503 backend that never closes, 3 attempts use 3 connections and the proxy closes all 3 (no leaked socket); the last 503 body is relayed.
